extracted.intended_audience: readers of Nature: professional scientists, naturalists, and educated public
extracted.subtask_description: A multidisciplinary early-20th Nature issue containing short news items, research summaries, methodological notes, and topical review articles (e.g., polar exploration, seismotectonics, aeroplane experiments).

rubrics_metrics.name: Polar exploration observational priorities
rubrics_metrics.description: Determination of the edge of the continental shelf; soundings to map the shelf edge; observations of temperature and salinity of deep-water strata beyond the shelf edge; equip sledging expeditions practically to do some oceanographical work where possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sledge journeys give little opportunity for soundings so include practical equipment when possible. A ship drift from the sea north of Bering Straits or western Alaska towards Greenland would provide important results and could likely be done in about five years (historical drift-cask example: Bryant and Melville took nearly six years from Alaska to Iceland).

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid overinterpreting ice-drift/current data as proof of land
rubrics_metrics.description: Ice-drift and surface-current observations alone cannot be taken as definitive evidence of land to the north; wind-driven drift and local conditions may mislead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depth soundings are essential before concluding the existence of land or continental shelf. Peary's and the Jeanette's drifts were influenced by winds and local ice conditions; tidal or ice-drift differences (e.g., Bennett Island vs Alaska) based on scanty observations are unreliable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seismotectonic mapping criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Damaged towns and villages tend to group along essentially parallel straight 'seismotectonic lines' related to coast-lines, mountain-mass borders, or geological-formation boundaries; the most seriously damaged places are generally at or near intersections of such lines; destructive intensity falls off rapidly perpendicular to these lines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conclude that destructive violence is localized on vertical planes of fracture in the crust which transmit seismic waves with least loss. Look for intersections with volcanotectonic lines (volcano alignments) and corroborative local phenomena (e.g., brontidi, mistpoeffers).

rubrics_metrics.name: Aeroplane design: prioritize longitudinal stability
rubrics_metrics.description: Longitudinal stability is of supreme importance in aeroplane design and should not be neglected in favor of other aims (such as building to win prizes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stability depends on additional factors such as the moment of inertia and the position of the centre of gravity of the apparatus; designers must consider these alongside aerodynamic data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aeroplane testing methodology (lift/pressure data)
rubrics_metrics.description: Laboratory experiments should measure forms and stability using planes and singly/doubly curved surfaces and plot curves showing lift, drift, and the coordinate of the centre of pressure as functions of angle of inclination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These data are useful for studying the stability of various types, but must be interpreted together with inertia and centre-of-gravity considerations to assess overall stability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Propeller design for maximum efficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: Propeller forms should be calculated/designed to give maximum efficiency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the theoretical and experimental analyses (e.g., Captain Ferber's notes) to guide propeller geometry and performance calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coal analysis method selection for certain Philippine coals
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard American Chemical Society directions for coal analyses may be inapplicable to some Philippine coals which shed incandescent carbon particles ('shower of incandescent carbon') when rapidly heated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detect such coals by this behaviour and avoid mechanical loss by expelling volatile matter very slowly so escaping gases do not ignite. The 'smoking-off' method (slow expulsion of volatiles) approximates coke-oven conditions and yields more appropriate results for these coal types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sugar-cane hybridisation methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: To produce improved sugar-cane varieties by hybridisation, remove anthers from young flowers and pollinate with pollen from a known type so that parentage can be determined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Earlier successes with seedling canes were fortuitous because parentage was unknown; controlled emasculation and pollination (as by Lewton-Brain, 1904) allow determination of parentage and systematic improvement. Papers should summarise results and indicate future research lines; illustrations of varieties are valuable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ceramics industry measurement and evaluation priorities
rubrics_metrics.description: Important topics to measure and control in ceramic/clay industries include: amount of soluble salts in clays, excess air in firing kilns, sulphuring and feathering of glazes, and the influence of high temperatures on porcelain pyrometer tubes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report methods for recording high temperatures and review different measuring approaches. Consider predictions for future kiln technology (e.g., gas firing) and include hygienic aspects of industrial practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use nomography/graphical methods for calculations
rubrics_metrics.description: Graphic methods of calculation (nomography) are effective for solving algebraic equations; simple devices such as squared paper can serve as substitutes for slide rules when used appropriately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prof. Maurice d'Ocagne's nomography principles are the basis; squared paper is noted as a simple and often overlooked practical substitute for more complex calculating instruments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Astronomical positional data reduction practice
rubrics_metrics.description: When publishing measured positions (e.g., of satellites like Phoebe), use standard-star positions appropriate to the epoch and include material so a second reduction can be performed if higher accuracy is later required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide standard-star places used (e.g., C.P.D. for epoch 1875.0) and include all observational material to allow future re-reduction by redetermining standard-star positions with greater accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spectral observation and classification standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Photographic stellar spectra should be classified and compared across epochs/observatories; note the presence and relative intensity of hydrogen series and absorption bands (e.g., Ha..H8) and identify elemental absorptions (e.g., vanadium).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare spectra from different maxima and observers (e.g., Lick vs Lowell results) and reproduce light-curves or spectral plates where useful for assessing variability and intensity changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication practice for museum and regional faunal works
rubrics_metrics.description: Museum and regional-fauna publications should aim to extend educational value by adding new local groups to exhibits and by providing corrected identifications, descriptions of new genera/species, figures, and maps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include corrections of previously recorded names, descriptions and figures of new taxa, and illustrative plates and maps to enhance the educational and scientific value of the work.
